title: Yoga and back pain
hookLine: for long-lasting low back pain, yoga helped about as well as other exercise (Cochrane review)

cards: Get up from a chair, and the lower back sends its usual message. Tie a shoe, and it sends another. Lift a bag of groceries out of the trunk: a third.
For people whose low back has ached for months, life fills up with these small negotiations. They try heat, pills, new mattresses and yoga mats.

A group of reviewers asked a plain question across all the trials they could gather: does yoga help a back like that, and how does it compare with other exercise? The answer is useful, and a little humbling for everyone.

teach.b: First, the review. A Cochrane review is a careful pooling of the trials on one question. This one looked at yoga for low back pain that had lasted a long time.
Compared with no exercise, yoga brought small improvements in pain and in how well people could move.

teach.h: ABOUT THE SAME AS OTHER EXERCISE.
teach.b: Compared with other kinds of exercise, there was little or no difference. The reviewers rated the evidence low to moderate in certainty, and noted some side effects, mostly more back pain, none serious.
Third, what that means. Yoga isn't a special cure for backs. It's one good way to move.
If yoga is what gets someone down on the floor and stretching, it's a fine choice. If a walk or a physical therapist's routine does that, so is that.
On this evidence, the name of the exercise matters less than doing some. Fourth, the word itself.

teach.h: ASANA: A SEAT, STEADY AND COMFORTABLE.
teach.b: In the Yoga Sutras, which tradition attributes to the sage Patanjali, asana means a seat, the posture for meditation, and the sutra asks that it be steady and comfortable.
Much of a modern yoga class, with standing poses and flowing sequences, looks different. Both belong to the story of yoga, and the Hindu tradition it grew from deserves to be named.
Steady and comfortable is still a good rule for a sore back.

how: People with ongoing back pain use yoga classes, walking or a physical therapist's exercises; in the Hindu yoga tradition, asana is the steady, comfortable seat for meditation.

games.q: your back has ached for months. one friend swears by yoga, another by walking and a physical therapy routine. in the Cochrane review, how did yoga compare with other exercise?
games.why: little or no difference. yoga beat no exercise by a small margin; on this evidence, moving matters more than which kind.

practice: Sitting where you are, roll your shoulders back slowly a few times, then turn gently to the right, one hand on the back of the chair, breathe, come back to center, and turn to the left.
If it's comfortable, fold forward a little and let your arms hang; steady and comfortable is the rule, so stop if anything is sharp. Then sit tall, hands in your lap, and rest.

wordCard.voice: Yoga and back pain. For long-lasting low back pain, yoga helped a little more than no exercise, and about as much as other exercise. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit, from the Hindu yoga tradition: a seat, a posture.

carryVoice: Your line: stretch. Any kind of moving counts, and back pain with numbness or weakness is a reason to call a doctor first. Go gently.

sources.ref: Wieland et al., "Yoga treatment for chronic non-specific low back pain" (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews)
